channel.title: The Daily Digest
channel.description: One top story from each of my chosen publications, updated daily.

item.title: NYT: In Elevating Stephen Miller, Trump Doubles Down on Hard-Line Agenda
item.description: The new White House chief of staff is responsible for some of the most provocative policies of President Trump’s second term, as well as an aggressive approach to executive power.

item.title: NPR: A promising new medicine against heart disease fails unexpectedly
item.description: Doctors expected an experimental drug that lowers a common risk factor for heart attacks would save patients' lives. The medicine made no difference.

item.title: BBC News: UK cannot 'cherry pick' EU single market deal, Barnier tells BBC
item.description: The former Brexit negotiator says EU countries would reject any British attempts to follow economic rules "a la carte".

item.title: The Guardian: In defense of feral children
item.description: Adults complain and say kids should occupy more space in the world. Then when they do, the world tells them to quiet down On the Maine island where I live, childhood ends when you’re old enough to catch the 7.15am ferry…

item.title: Al Jazeera: Iran’s IRGC says building underground sites for weapons production, storage
item.description: IRGC says underground military complexes allow missile production to continue even under heavy bombardment.

item.title: Ars Technica: The Bantu expansion changed Africa. Scientists are still tracing how.
item.description: Genes and archaeology are revealing how Bantu speakers spread across much of Africa.

item.title: WIRED Backchannel: ‘Our Risk, Their Reward’: Zohran Mamdani on AI and Data Centers
item.description: Ahead of the midterms, WIRED talked to New York City’s mayor about data centers, AI in schools, and the future of the Democratic party.

item.title: WIRED Science: The American Dream Wasn’t Built for Climate Change
item.description: Owning a home is billed as a way to build wealth, but amid climate-related disasters, for many, it's beginning to feel like a trap.

item.title: WIRED Business: AI Companies Really, Really Want to Buy Your Work Files and Emails
item.description: Data brokers are collecting all sorts of internal corporate files to help train AI models. Not everyone is thrilled.

item.title: The New Yorker: Breaking the Decade-Long Trump Fever
item.description: The President’s unique brand of lurid authoritarianism has finally lost appeal, and he has lost the plot.

item.title: New York Mag The Cut: The Woman Having Sex on the Floor at a Bar
item.description: In this week’s story, her date lays down a clean tablecloth first.

item.title: New York Mag Curbed: So Long, Cybertruck
item.description: Tesla’s behemoth became a stainless-steel white elephant.

item.description: INDIANAPOLIS - An investigation is underway after a man was killed in a stabbing on Indy's south side Saturday morning. According to the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department, officers responded to the 2300 block o…

item.title: Mirror Indy: What voters want after Democrats’ big gains in Indiana
item.description: Anger at Trump helped Democrats flip at least 16 seats in the Indiana House. The post What voters want after Democrats’ big gains in Indiana appeared first on Mirror Indy .
